title: Understanding a Contract
text:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. For a contract to be valid, it usually needs an offer, an acceptance, and consideration, which means that each party gives something of value. Parties must also have the legal capacity to sign, and the agreement must have a lawful purpose.

If one party breaks the terms of the contract, the other party may seek a remedy, such as financial compensation or a court order. Many contracts include a clause that explains how disputes will be resolved. Some agreements require mediation before the parties can go to court. Reading a contract carefully before signing can prevent costly misunderstandings.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is a contract?
options: A legally binding agreement between parties
A document that only one party must sign
A promise that cannot be enforced

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what can the other party seek if the contract is broken?
options: A new contract with different terms
Financial compensation or a court order
A signed letter from a lawyer
A shorter length for the contract

questions.text: Why does the author recommend reading a contract carefully before signing?
options: Because contracts are always written in court
Because it can help avoid expensive misunderstandings
Because mediation is always required by law

questions.text: What can be inferred about a contract that has no clause explaining how disputes are resolved?
options: Disagreements might be harder to settle clearly

paragraph_translations: Un contrato es un acuerdo legalmente vinculante entre dos o más partes. Para que un contrato sea válido, normalmente necesita una oferta, una aceptación y una contraprestación, lo que significa que cada parte entrega algo de valor. Las partes también deben tener capacidad legal para firmar, y el acuerdo debe tener un propósito lícito.

Si una parte incumple los términos del contrato, la otra parte puede buscar un recurso legal, como una compensación económica o una orden judicial. Muchos contratos incluyen una cláusula que explica cómo se resolverán las disputas. Algunos acuerdos exigen mediación antes de que las partes puedan acudir a los tribunales. Leer un contrato con atención antes de firmarlo puede evitar malentendidos costosos.
